newsitem.title: USA: Accused North Carolina serial killer to stand trial.
newsitem.headline: Accused North Carolina serial killer to stand trial.

text.p: A former fast food worker accused of using brassieres and bath towels to strangle nine North Carolina women will go on trial next week after defence lawyers Monday declined to ask for a continuance.

Lawyers for accused serial killer Henry Wallace said they were ready to present the case as scheduled Sept. 30 even though they did not have results from Wallace's DNA tests and had not viewed the alleged crime scenes. "We're ready for the case to start," Public Defender Isabelle Day said.

Wallace is accused of killing 10 women in Charlotte between 1992 and 1994 but the trial is for nine counts of first-degree murder for strangling women with their bras or bathroom towels during an alleged two-year murder spree while he was addicted to crack cocaine.
The 30-year-old former fast food worker was arrested in March 1994 and charged with Charlotte's worst killing spree. His lawyers would not say if he would take the witness stand.
Prosecutors are seeking the death penalty on each count if jurors find Wallace guilty of first-degree murder.
Wallace knew the murdered women and allegedly raped some of them, making DNA, the basic material in cells containing genetic code, a key factor in the case.

North Carolina Superior Court Judge Robert Johnston delayed rulings on three issues including whether Wallace's audiotaped confession to police can be copied by two local television stations. The judge opposed a similar request when the tapes were initially played during a hearing last year.
Day said she was concerned about the "overwhelming" amount of publicity in the case and she would file a motion for a change of venue by next week.

Jury selection was expected to last three weeks. The judge said it would get underway only when both sides were ready. There will be a primary panel of 12 but a numebr of alternates not yet been fixed.
The trial was expected to last eight weeks.
